title: case-sensitive needs more text

labels.name: i18n-needs-resolution
labels.description: Issue the Internationalization Group has raised and looks for a response on.

body:
Case sensitivity and string comparison [HTML]
https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/infrastructure.html#case-sensitivity-and-string-comparison

> 2.2 Case-sensitivity and string comparison
>Comparing two strings in a case-sensitive manner means comparing them exactly, code point for code point.
>Except where otherwise stated, string comparisons must be performed in a case-sensitive manner.
>A string pattern is a prefix match for a string s when pattern is not longer than s and truncating s to pattern's length leaves the two strings as matches of each other.

In recent weeks, I18N WG has encountered a couple of specifications [[1]](https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/4452)[[2]](https://github.com/whatwg/dom/issues/793) referring to the above definition of "case-sensitive". 

The I18N WG agrees without reservation with how case-sensitive matching is defined here.

However, the implications of code point by code point comparison are not mentioned in HTML and thus seem to be being overlooked by other specification authors. We suggest that there be a health warning included into section 2.2, possibly referring to our detailed document [Charmod-Norm](https://www.w3.org/TR/charmod-norm/). Perhaps something like:

> Note: code point for code point comparison is not just sensitive to case variation but also to other variations in how Unicode strings can be encoded, such as normalization form. These differences are invisible and can occur between strings that Unicode considers "canonically equivalent". For more information see [Charmod-Norm].
